lines.en: Hi Omar! You look puzzled. What is on your mind?
Hi Sara. My manager wrote that my proposal was interesting, which, coming from him, is usually a polite way of saying no.
What he did not say in that email probably speaks louder than anything he actually said.
Exactly. It is one thing to say you agree, and quite another to mean it.
So how will you reply?
That is my problem. The reply must be formal, and I only know how to write to friends.
However brilliant your idea may be, presenting it in the wrong register can kill it before anyone listens.
True. Were the letter written to a friend rather than a manager, its tone would be entirely different.
Start with something careful. It would seem that the data point in one direction, though they are far from conclusive.
Good. And I should add that further studies are needed before any firm conclusion.
Now you sound like a scientist. What cautious writers understand is that a well-placed 'perhaps' can be more persuasive than a bold claim.
My old teacher never hedged. He tended to overstate his case, which is why his otherwise good arguments were often dismissed.
Speaking of your old teacher, is he the one who only spoke in idioms?
The very one. He always said it is no use crying over spilled milk; what matters is how we fix the situation.
What makes idioms so difficult is that their meaning rarely has anything to do with their words.
He told me once: were I in your shoes, I would think twice before burning any bridges.
Wise advice. And how is the debate club going, by the way?
Hard. What distinguishes a strong argument from a loud one is the quality of its evidence, not its volume.
Some people never learn that. It is a common mistake to attack the person instead of the argument.
Admittedly, my opponent's plan had its strengths; nevertheless, it ignored the single most important risk.
Not until both sides agree on the facts can any real debate about solutions begin.
However appealing a slogan may sound, it is no substitute for a well-reasoned policy.
You sound ready for the final round.
I hope so. To claim that technology alone will solve our problems is to misunderstand what the problems are.
That is a strong closing line. Rarely does anyone win a debate by shouting; they simply lose the audience.
And if I lose, at least I will not cry over spilled milk.
That is the spirit. Now go and write that formal reply.
Should you require my best formal English, you will find it in your inbox tonight.
Was that a joke in formal register? I am impressed!
Not until you have written the same message in three different styles do you understand what register really means.
